scr_ap_printing_a_list_of_a_p_invoices.purpose: Filters the A/P invoices list to a defined population — property, state, date range — and exports it to PDF or Excel so the printed register becomes the support packet that travels with a check run to the onshore reviewer and into the month-end work papers.
scr_ap_printing_a_list_of_a_p_invoices.outcome: A dated, filtered invoice register that a reviewer can sign against and that ties to the 2010 Accounts Payable control balance as of the moment it was run.
scr_ap_printing_a_list_of_a_p_invoices.rootCause: An invoice register is a point-in-time snapshot of a liability that keeps moving. If the offshore team runs it Monday and a site batch posts Tuesday, the register the reviewer signs understates the owner's committed cash, and nobody discovers the gap until the aging is tied to the trial balance at close.
scr_ap_printing_a_list_of_a_p_invoices.ifSkipped: The check run goes out with no independent record of what was proposed, and the reviewer has nothing to compare the disbursement against afterward.
gaap: COSO 2013 — information and communication; review evidence
SOC 1 — resident and vendor data leaving the application boundary
redFlags: Register printed without the run date and filter criteria on the face of it
Draft-only filter left applied so posted invoices are missing from the packet
Exported register emailed outside the SOC 1 environment with vendor bank detail visible
scr_ap_printing_a_list_of_a_p_invoices.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find with filters, then Excel export; or Analytics > Payable Analytics > Payable Register for the formatted list.

scr_ap_creating_a_multi_entity_invoice.purpose: Enters one vendor invoice whose cost belongs to several legal entities by adding a line per entity in the Location column with that entity's share in Price, so a single landscaping or insurance bill splits across the properties that consumed it.
scr_ap_creating_a_multi_entity_invoice.outcome: One payable to the vendor, with each entity carrying its own expense debit and its own share of the liability, and the paying entity's advance recorded as an affiliate receivable.
scr_ap_creating_a_multi_entity_invoice.rootCause: Shared-service vendors invoice the management company or one property for work performed across a portfolio. Splitting the invoice is the only way each owner's operating statement carries its true cost; the allocation basis (unit count, square feet, actual service tickets) must be the one in the management agreement, because an arbitrary split means one entity is subsidizing another's expense.
scr_ap_creating_a_multi_entity_invoice.ifSkipped: The whole cost lands on one property, that owner's NOI is understated and the sister entity's is overstated, and the correcting reclass has to be explained to two different owners.
gaap: ASC 850 — related-party transactions and disclosure
ASC 810 — entities under common control
COSO 2013 — authorization of intercompany allocations
redFlags: Allocation percentages that do not match the basis in the management agreement
Due From / Due To balances that never net to zero across the portfolio
One entity consistently absorbing the rounding difference
Multi-entity invoices entered by a single preparer with no second review
scr_ap_creating_a_multi_entity_invoice.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable Entry with detail lines coded to different properties, generating Due To/Due From via Setup > Intercompany Accounts; or an Expense Pool allocation of the shared invoice.

scr_ap_checking_the_status_of_an_a_p_inv.purpose: Reads the State column on the A/P invoices list — Draft, Draft selected, Partially approved, Selected, Partially paid, Posted — to determine whether a specific invoice has reached the general ledger, is stalled in approval, or is merely queued for the next payment run.
scr_ap_checking_the_status_of_an_a_p_inv.outcome: A definite answer on where one invoice sits, and whether its expense is already in the period's results or still outside them.
scr_ap_checking_the_status_of_an_a_p_inv.rootCause: Status is the dividing line between an expense that is in the numbers and one that is not. An invoice sitting at Partially approved on the last day of the month has been received, has a known amount and a known service period, but has posted nothing — that is precisely the population that becomes the missed accrual to 2020 Accrued Expenses when the offshore team closes without sweeping it.
scr_ap_checking_the_status_of_an_a_p_inv.ifSkipped: Approved-but-unposted invoices are left out of the accrual, the property's expenses are understated for the month, and the catch-up lands in the next period's variance explanation.
gaap: ASC 720 — expense recognition when the service is received
COSO 2013 — completeness of period-end cut-off
reports: A/P invoices list filtered by state
redFlags: Invoices stuck at Partially approved past the accrual cut-off
Draft invoices dated in a prior period that nobody has cleared
Partially paid status on invoices the vendor believes are settled in full
scr_ap_checking_the_status_of_an_a_p_inv.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find showing payable status (unposted/posted/paid) and PAYscan workflow position on the invoice register.

scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice.purpose: Removes an A/P invoice outright from the Invoice Research results using the Delete check box, available only where the record is eligible; where it is not, the Reverse link is offered instead because posted history cannot simply disappear.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice.outcome: A genuinely erroneous invoice leaves the system, or the accountant is forced onto the reversal path that preserves the audit trail.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice.rootCause: Invoice Research reaches records across a wide search, which makes it the easiest place to delete the wrong thing. RealPage deliberately withholds Delete where the invoice has posted or paid, because removing a posted liability silently changes a closed period's expenses without leaving anything an auditor can follow.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice.ifSkipped: Duplicate keyed invoices accumulate in the aging, the vendor balance overstates what is owed, and a second payment eventually goes out against the phantom.
gaap: COSO 2013 — audit trail retention over voided and deleted records
Record retention under the management agreement and owner audit rights
redFlags: Delete used where Reverse was available, erasing the history
Deletion of an invoice that already has an asset record attached — the asset survives and orphans
Deletions performed by the same user who keyed the invoice
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find > delete an unposted payable; posted payables are reversed instead, which keeps both entries in the ledger.

scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details.purpose: Opens the Approval Workflow Document PDF attached to an invoice when RealPage is integrated with OPSTechnology, showing each approval step, approver and timestamp alongside the scanned invoice image in one artifact.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details.outcome: A single retrievable document proving who authorized a specific payable and against which invoice image.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details.rootCause: When invoice approval happens in an external platform, the approval evidence lives outside the accounting system. Auditors testing authorization controls ask for the approval trail on a sample of payables; if the workflow document cannot be produced from the invoice record itself, the control is untested and the sample becomes an exception.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details.ifSkipped: Authorization for material payables cannot be evidenced at audit, and the owner's approval matrix is effectively unenforceable.
gaap: COSO 2013 — control activities, evidence of authorization
SOC 1 — complementary user entity controls over approvals
redFlags: Workflow documents showing submitter and approver as the same person
IRN field blank on high-dollar invoices, meaning no workflow record exists
Approvals recorded after the payment date
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan invoice register showing the workflow trail and approval history per payable, with the scanned image attached via Document Management.

scr_ap_invoice_research_list.purpose: A search-first invoice workspace that shows nothing until criteria are entered, then exposes view, edit, delete, reverse, print, pay, package, import and export against the matched invoices across the whole portfolio.
scr_ap_invoice_research_list.outcome: A targeted result set for a specific question — a vendor dispute, a duplicate check, an auditor's sample — with the actions to resolve it in the same place.
scr_ap_invoice_research_list.rootCause: The standard A/P invoices list defaults to a recent window and one working scope; research questions do not. When a vendor calls about an invoice from eight months ago at a property the accountant does not normally cover, the only way to answer is a query that ignores the default filters — and the same breadth means an unwary action here reaches records the accountant never intended to touch.
scr_ap_invoice_research_list.ifSkipped: Vendor inquiries and duplicate-payment investigations are answered from the limited default list, so older or out-of-scope invoices are declared not to exist.
gaap: COSO 2013 — monitoring and investigation of exceptions
SOC 1 — logical access scoped by property
redFlags: Users with research permissions across entities they do not support
Bulk actions taken on a broad result set without narrowing first
Searches by amount only, which collides across unrelated vendors
scr_ap_invoice_research_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find (cross-property search by vendor, invoice number, amount and date) with the same edit, void and pay actions on the results.

scr_ap_printing_invoices_from_the_invoic.purpose: Prints an individual invoice to PDF straight from a research result, used when a vendor disputes a charge, an owner questions a line on the operating statement, or an auditor pulls a specific payable from a sample.
scr_ap_printing_invoices_from_the_invoic.outcome: A clean printed copy of the invoice as recorded, deliverable to whoever raised the question without giving them access to the system.
scr_ap_printing_invoices_from_the_invoic.rootCause: Disputes are settled with the document, not with a screen. Printing from research is how the offshore team answers a query about a property and period outside its normal window, and the print reflects the record as coded — which is exactly why a printed copy that disagrees with the vendor's original is the signal that the coding or the amount was keyed wrong.
scr_ap_printing_invoices_from_the_invoic.ifSkipped: Vendor disputes drag on with screenshots and verbal amounts, and the auditor's sample request is answered late or incompletely.
gaap: COSO 2013 — supporting documentation for recorded transactions
SOC 1 — controlled distribution of invoice documents
redFlags: Printed invoice totals disagreeing with the attached vendor image
Invoices printed and circulated while still in Draft state
No attachment behind the printed record for a material payable
scr_ap_printing_invoices_from_the_invoic.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find > open the payable and print, or retrieve the PAYscan scanned image from Document Management.

scr_ap_paying_invoices_from_the_invoice_.purpose: Jumps from a researched invoice straight to Pay A/P Invoices and issues payment on it, the route used when a single invoice must move outside the scheduled run — a lien deadline, a shutoff notice, a vendor holding a make-ready.
scr_ap_paying_invoices_from_the_invoice_.outcome: One targeted invoice is paid without disturbing the batch, and the invoice closes against the bank it was drawn on.
scr_ap_paying_invoices_from_the_invoice_.rootCause: Paying from a search bypasses the discipline of the weekly proposal, where available cash, vendor holds and owner funding are reviewed together. The payment is legitimate, but it draws on property cash that the cash forecast has already committed elsewhere, so the off-cycle disbursement must be reflected before the next run is built.
scr_ap_paying_invoices_from_the_invoice_.ifSkipped: Time-critical payments miss their deadline, the property incurs late fees or a mechanic's lien filing, and services are interrupted at an occupied asset.
gaap: COSO 2013 — authorization of non-routine disbursements
State mechanic's lien statutes — payment timing and lien waiver exchange
NACHA Operating Rules — off-cycle ACH origination
redFlags: Off-cycle payments released without the approval a batch would have required
Same invoice paid here and again in the scheduled run
Payments drawn against a property with no available cash, creating an overdraft
scr_ap_paying_invoices_from_the_invoice_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find > select the payable and run Check Processing / Manual Check against it individually.

scr_ap_viewing_the_status_of_a_payment_o.purpose: Reads the Payment status column on the Posted Payments list to tell whether a disbursement or refund was submitted, succeeded, failed or was returned, filtering by vendor name or payment method to isolate the item in question.
scr_ap_viewing_the_status_of_a_payment_o.outcome: Certainty about whether the money actually left the account, which is the fact the bank reconciliation and the vendor both depend on.
scr_ap_viewing_the_status_of_a_payment_o.rootCause: An ACH that failed at the bank looks identical to one that succeeded on the invoice record — the invoice closes either way. Until the payment status is read, the accountant believes the vendor is paid, the vendor believes it is not, and the cash never left, so the bank reconciliation carries a reconciling item nobody can explain.
scr_ap_viewing_the_status_of_a_payment_o.ifSkipped: Failed and returned payments sit undetected, vendors escalate to collections, and the reconciliation carries unexplained differences until someone traces them individually.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — return codes and re-origination timing
COSO 2013 — monitoring of disbursement completeness
redFlags: Failed ACH payments with the invoice still showing Paid
Returned payments not re-originated within the vendor's terms
Refund status never followed through to receipt of funds
scr_ap_viewing_the_status_of_a_payment_o.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Register / EFT history showing payment and ACH return status per disbursement.

scr_ap_posted_payments_list.purpose: The register of payments that have actually posted, defaulted to the last 90 days by payment date, from which details, attachments, printed copies, vendor notices, voids and exports are all launched.
scr_ap_posted_payments_list.outcome: A single authoritative list of money disbursed in the recent window, usable as the starting point for reconciliation, vendor queries and voids.
scr_ap_posted_payments_list.rootCause: The 90-day default window is the trap. A stale check from five months ago, a duplicate payment from last quarter, an escheatment candidate — none of them appear until the filter is widened, so an accountant who works only the default view concludes the disbursement history is complete when it is merely recent.
scr_ap_posted_payments_list.ifSkipped: Older payments are invisible to routine review, aged outstanding checks never surface for stop-payment or escheatment, and duplicate-payment recoveries go unpursued.
gaap: State unclaimed property (escheat) statutes — aged uncashed checks
COSO 2013 — periodic review of disbursements
redFlags: Reviews performed only within the 90-day default
Payments to vendors with no invoice link
Uncashed checks aged past the state dormancy period with no escheat action
scr_ap_posted_payments_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Register (filtered by bank, property and date range) with void, reprint and export actions on the results.

scr_ap_printing_a_posted_payment.purpose: Produces a printed or saved-as-PDF record of one posted payment via Print copy — a non-negotiable copy showing payee, amount, date, bank and the invoices it settled.
scr_ap_printing_a_posted_payment.outcome: A physical or PDF payment record that can be filed with the disbursement support or sent to a vendor claiming non-receipt.
scr_ap_printing_a_posted_payment.rootCause: The printed copy is what settles a vendor's claim that they were never paid — it names the check number and date the vendor can take to their own bank. It is deliberately non-negotiable so that a copy circulating in email cannot be presented for deposit, which matters because payment copies get forwarded well outside the accounting team.
scr_ap_printing_a_posted_payment.ifSkipped: Vendor non-receipt claims cannot be rebutted, unnecessary stop-payments and reissues are processed, and the same obligation gets paid twice.
gaap: UCC Article 3 — negotiability of instruments and copies
COSO 2013 — documentation of disbursements
redFlags: Copies printed on live check stock
Payment copies emailed with the full bank account number visible
Copies issued for payments that were subsequently voided
scr_ap_printing_a_posted_payment.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Register > reprint a check copy (non-negotiable) or produce the remittance advice for the vendor.

scr_ap_saving_a_pdf_copy_of_a_payment.purpose: Downloads the payment copy as a PDF to the accountant's own machine through the Download button on the Print copy preview, rather than routing it to a printer.
scr_ap_saving_a_pdf_copy_of_a_payment.outcome: A portable payment document available for attachment to an owner package, an audit response or a vendor email.
scr_ap_saving_a_pdf_copy_of_a_payment.rootCause: The moment the PDF lands on a local drive it is outside the application's access controls and its audit log. It carries payee, bank account and amount, so a downloaded payment copy sitting in a shared folder or a personal Downloads directory is an unmonitored copy of disbursement data — the exact exposure the offshore delivery model's SOC 1 boundary is meant to prevent.
scr_ap_saving_a_pdf_copy_of_a_payment.ifSkipped: Payment evidence has to be reproduced from the system for every request, slowing audit and owner responses to a crawl.
gaap: SOC 1 — data leaving the service organization's controlled environment
COSO 2013 — information handling and retention
redFlags: Payment PDFs stored on personal drives instead of the document repository
Downloads of payment copies in bulk with no business request behind them
Files named so vaguely that they cannot be tied back to a check number
scr_ap_saving_a_pdf_copy_of_a_payment.yardi: Yardi Voyager: export or save the check copy / remittance advice as PDF, with the controlled copy retained in Document Management.

scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_details.purpose: Opens one posted payment and its linked context — the vendor record, each invoice it settled, the History tab of completed events, the audit trail of changes, and the email payment notice action.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_details.outcome: The full chain behind a single disbursement, from vendor master to invoices to the people who touched it.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_details.rootCause: A disbursement question is almost never about the payment alone; it is about which invoices it covered and whether the remit-to it used was the vendor's legitimate one. Opening the detail is how a suspected fraudulent payment is tested, because the audit trail shows whether the vendor's bank details were altered shortly before the payment was released.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_details.ifSkipped: Payment inquiries are answered from the summary line, invoice-level disputes stay unresolved, and vendor-bank-change fraud goes undetected.
gaap: COSO 2013 — fraud risk assessment over disbursements
SOC 1 — change logging on master data used in payments
redFlags: Vendor bank details changed within days of the payment
Payments covering invoices from a property outside the payer entity with no intercompany entry
Audit trail showing the payment amount edited after submission
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_details.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check > open the check to see the paid payables detail, with the record's History/Audit function for change logging.

scr_ap_printing_a_copy_of_a_payment.purpose: The Print copy page itself, which renders a non-negotiable duplicate of a check or electronic payment issued from Accounts Payable or Cash Management and also offers to send the payment notification email from the same place.
scr_ap_printing_a_copy_of_a_payment.outcome: A viewable, printable, downloadable payment copy plus the option to notify the vendor directly, without leaving the payment record.
scr_ap_printing_a_copy_of_a_payment.rootCause: Combining the copy and the vendor notification on one page matters operationally: most requests for a payment copy come from a vendor who has not been notified, and sending the notice resolves the inquiry without the copy ever leaving the building. It also means the notification can be fired accidentally while someone is only trying to view the document.
scr_ap_printing_a_copy_of_a_payment.ifSkipped: Vendor payment inquiries consume A/P time that automated notification would have eliminated, and payment copies get produced manually for every call.
gaap: UCC Article 3 — non-negotiable copies of instruments
NACHA Operating Rules — remittance detail accompanying ACH credits
redFlags: Notification emails going to a stale vendor contact address
Copies produced for voided payments and sent to vendors as proof
Payment notices sent for payments that later failed at the bank
scr_ap_printing_a_copy_of_a_payment.yardi: Yardi Voyager: reprint the check copy from the Check Register and email the remittance advice to the vendor's payment contact.

scr_ap_posted_payment_page.purpose: The detail page for a posted payment with two tabs — Payment information listing bank, method, amount and the invoices covered with attachment links, and History logging the transaction's lifecycle from creation to payment.
scr_ap_posted_payment_page.outcome: One screen that answers what was paid, from which account, against which invoices, and by whom at each step.
scr_ap_posted_payment_page.rootCause: The invoice links on this page are the mechanism for tying disbursements back to the liability they extinguished. Without walking them, an accountant reconciling 2010 Accounts Payable cannot prove that the debit side of a payment relieved real, approved payables rather than posting straight to expense or on account.
scr_ap_posted_payment_page.ifSkipped: Cash disbursements cannot be traced to the payables they cleared, and the A/P subledger-to-GL reconciliation carries differences with no explanation.
gaap: COSO 2013 — transaction traceability from disbursement to obligation
ASC 405 — derecognition of a liability when settled
redFlags: Payments with no invoices in the detail section
Attachment links that open nothing for material payments
History showing submit, approve and confirm by a single user
scr_ap_posted_payment_page.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check detail listing the paid payables, with the History/Audit function for the lifecycle log.

scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_attachm.purpose: Opens the scanned backup attached to an invoice from inside a posted payment record, using the Attachment button in the Invoices section, so the source document can be read without navigating back to the invoice.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_attachm.outcome: The vendor's original document is visible in the same context as the money that paid it.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_attachm.rootCause: Reaching the attachment from the payment is how an accountant tests that the amount disbursed matches the document the vendor actually sent. When an auditor samples cash disbursements, the required evidence is the invoice image behind the payment — not the keyed record, which can be wrong in exactly the way the test is designed to catch.
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_attachm.ifSkipped: Cash disbursement testing fails for want of source documents, and overpayments against altered or inflated invoices are never caught.
gaap: COSO 2013 — supporting documentation retained with the transaction
SOC 1 — document retention within the service boundary
redFlags: Material payments whose invoices carry no attachment at all
Attachment amounts differing from the keyed invoice total
Statements attached in place of invoices, which cannot support a specific charge
scr_ap_viewing_a_posted_payments_attachm.yardi: Yardi Voyager: open the check, drill to the paid payable and open its Document Management attachment (PAYscan invoice image).

scr_ap_viewing_payment_history.purpose: Opens the History tab on a posted payment to see who selected the item for payment, who approved it and who confirmed it, each with its timestamp.
scr_ap_viewing_payment_history.outcome: A named, dated sequence of the people who moved a disbursement from selection to release.
scr_ap_viewing_payment_history.rootCause: Segregation of duties in A/P is only real if it can be demonstrated after the fact, and this tab is where it is demonstrated. The manual's own example shows submit, approve and confirm all performed by one user — which is the textbook control failure in an offshore delivery model where a small team covers many properties and one person quietly ends up holding every step.
scr_ap_viewing_payment_history.ifSkipped: Segregation-of-duties failures stay invisible until an auditor samples payments or a fraud is discovered, by which point months of disbursements share the same defect.
gaap: COSO 2013 — segregation of duties and control activity evidence
SOC 1 — user access review over payment roles
redFlags: Same user recorded as submitter, approver and confirmer
Approval timestamps after the payment confirmation
Approvals clustered at odd hours by one account across many properties
scr_ap_viewing_payment_history.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the History/Audit function on the check record plus Administration > User Activity reports for the approval sequence.

scr_ap_printing_the_proof_of_payment_fro.purpose: Generates a proof-of-payment PDF from a paid or partially paid A/P invoice through the Proof of Payment button on the invoice edit page, producing the document that evidences settlement of that specific obligation.
scr_ap_printing_the_proof_of_payment_fro.outcome: A downloadable PDF tying the invoice to the payment that discharged it, suitable for sending to a vendor or a lien claimant.
scr_ap_printing_the_proof_of_payment_fro.rootCause: Proof of payment is what releases a lien claim. A subcontractor or supplier who has not been paid by the general contractor can file against the property even though the owner paid the GC in full, and the owner's defence is documentary — the proof of payment plus the lien waiver. Producing it from the invoice, not the payment, is what ties the evidence to the exact obligation in dispute.
scr_ap_printing_the_proof_of_payment_fro.ifSkipped: A paid-twice or lien exposure cannot be rebutted with documents, and the property pays again to clear a claim it already settled.
gaap: State mechanic's lien statutes — proof of payment and lien waiver evidence
COSO 2013 — documentation supporting settled obligations
redFlags: Proof of payment issued on partially paid invoices without stating the balance
No matching conditional or unconditional lien waiver on file
Proofs produced for payments later voided
scr_ap_printing_the_proof_of_payment_fro.yardi: Yardi Voyager: retrieve the check detail for the payable and produce the check copy/remittance as proof, with lien waivers filed in Document Management.

scr_ap_voiding_multiple_payments.purpose: Voids up to 50 posted payments at once from the Posted Payments list, setting a single void date and optional memo and choosing per payment whether the underlying invoices reverse at the same time.
scr_ap_voiding_multiple_payments.outcome: A batch of bad or stale payments is reversed in one action, with a consistent void date and a documented reason.
scr_ap_voiding_multiple_payments.rootCause: Bulk voiding applies one void date to fifty payments that may span several periods. If that date lands in a period already reported to the owner, the reversal rewrites a closed month's cash; if the invoice reversal box is left unchecked, the payables reopen and are eligible for the very next check run, which is how a bulk void turns into a bulk duplicate payment.
scr_ap_voiding_multiple_payments.ifSkipped: Stale and erroneous checks stay outstanding on the bank reconciliation indefinitely and eventually become unclaimed property obligations.
gaap: COSO 2013 — authorization and period control over reversals
State unclaimed property statutes — stale-dated instruments
UCC Article 4 — stale-dated checks and stop-payment
redFlags: Void date falling in a closed or already-reported period
Checks voided without confirming against the bank portal that they have not cleared
Invoice reversal box left unchecked, silently reopening the payables
Bulk voids with no memo explaining the reason
scr_ap_voiding_multiple_payments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check > Void Check per check (with the option to reverse the payable), or a bulk void via the Check Register selection.

scr_ap_overview_of_applying_credit_to_in.purpose: Explains how vendor advances and credit adjustments are applied against open A/P invoices on the Pay A/P Invoices page — either auto-applied to the oldest charge or directed line by line through the Line details link.
scr_ap_overview_of_applying_credit_to_in.outcome: Understanding of which credits offset which charges, so a payment nets correctly instead of paying in full alongside an unused credit.
scr_ap_overview_of_applying_credit_to_in.rootCause: Auto-application to the oldest charge is convenient and frequently wrong. A vendor credit for a specific over-billed unit turn belongs against that line and that property; letting it land on the oldest open invoice moves the benefit to a different GL account and often a different entity, so two operating statements are misstated by the credit amount and the original dispute stays unresolved.
scr_ap_overview_of_applying_credit_to_in.ifSkipped: Credits sit unused on the vendor account while invoices are paid gross, tying up property cash and eventually escheating as vendor overpayments.
gaap: ASC 405 — offsetting and derecognition of liabilities
COSO 2013 — accuracy of application against the correct obligation
redFlags: Aged unapplied credits sitting on active vendor accounts
Credits auto-applied across properties or entities
Credit amount applied without the vendor's credit memo attached
scr_ap_overview_of_applying_credit_to_in.yardi: Yardi Voyager: enter the credit as a negative payable and apply it during Check Processing, or offset directly on the payable detail.

scr_ap_reclassifying_an_a_p_invoice_paid.purpose: Recodes the system-generated A/P invoice that a manual payment creates — the GL accounts, properties and line splits can change, while date, total and vendor are locked because they describe money that already moved.
scr_ap_reclassifying_an_a_p_invoice_paid.outcome: A wire or hand check keyed under time pressure ends up coded to the right expense accounts and properties without disturbing the cash record.
scr_ap_reclassifying_an_a_p_invoice_paid.rootCause: Manual payments are made in an emergency — a utility shutoff, an insurance binder, a tax deadline — and whoever cuts them codes to whatever account is nearest. Reclassify exists because the cash side is correct and immutable while the expense side is usually not, and a wrong code on a six-figure tax or insurance wire distorts the property's operating statement and its budget variance for the whole year.
scr_ap_reclassifying_an_a_p_invoice_paid.ifSkipped: Emergency payments stay coded to a catch-all account, the owner's variance commentary is built on wrong expense lines, and the error compounds every month the wire recurs.
gaap: COSO 2013 — accuracy of account classification
ASC 720 — classification of operating expenses
redFlags: Reclass attempted to change the amount or vendor, which forces a void and re-entry
Tax and insurance wires left in 6410 Administrative
Reclasses posted into a period already reported to the owner
scr_ap_reclassifying_an_a_p_invoice_paid.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Manual Check creating the payable, then edit the payable's GL detail or post a reclassifying journal entry.

scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list_2.purpose: The working A/P invoices list with its own controls — Include private for entity-level invoices, the last-90-days limiter, Show future draft invoices, the Hold indicator, the State column with links into approval history, and package selection.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list_2.outcome: A configurable view of the invoice population that reflects whatever the accountant actually needs to see, including the records the defaults hide.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list_2.rootCause: Three defaults on this list each hide something material: the 90-day window hides old open payables, Include private governs whether entity-level invoices appear at all, and future drafts are excluded unless requested. A saved view that quietly drops on-hold or entity-level invoices is how an approver signs off on a check run that is missing part of the liability.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list_2.ifSkipped: The invoice population under review is incomplete, aged payables and entity-level invoices escape attention, and the aging never agrees with the control account.
gaap: COSO 2013 — completeness of the population under review
ASC 810 — visibility of entity-level activity in a consolidated structure
redFlags: Custom views that exclude on-hold invoices
Include private cleared so entity-level invoices vanish from the review
Open invoices older than 90 days invisible under the default filter
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Find with saved filter sets and column configuration, plus the on-hold flag on each payable.

scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoice_messaging.purpose: Opens the Messaging tab on an A/P invoice to read the chat history — the exchange between site staff, approvers and the offshore team about coding questions, missing backup, disputed amounts and hold reasons.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoice_messaging.outcome: The reasoning behind an invoice's treatment is visible next to the invoice itself rather than trapped in email.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoice_messaging.rootCause: In an offshore delivery model the person who coded an invoice, the person who approved it and the person who reviews it at close are in different time zones and rarely speak. The messaging thread is the only written record of why a repair was capitalized rather than expensed, or why an invoice sat on hold through a period end — and that reasoning is exactly what an auditor asks for when testing capitalization judgments.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoice_messaging.ifSkipped: The rationale for judgment calls lives in individual inboxes, and when the preparer moves on nobody can defend the treatment of a capitalized repair or a held invoice.
gaap: ASC 360 — capitalization versus expense judgments and their support
COSO 2013 — communication supporting control decisions
redFlags: Coding disputes resolved in email with nothing recorded on the invoice
Capitalization decisions with no stated reasoning in the thread
Threads showing an approver instructing a change in coding to stay within budget
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoice_messaging.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan workflow comments and payable notes, plus Document Management attachments carrying correspondence.

scr_ap_reversing_an_a_p_invoice.purpose: Reverses a posted A/P invoice on a chosen transaction date with a required memo, available only when reversal of unpaid invoices is enabled in the Accounts Payable configuration.
scr_ap_reversing_an_a_p_invoice.outcome: The liability and its expense are backed out in a stated period, with both the original and the reversal visible in the ledger.
scr_ap_reversing_an_a_p_invoice.rootCause: The choice of reversal date is the whole control. Reversing into the original period rewrites results the owner has already received; reversing into the current open period leaves the original expense in the month it hit and corrects it prospectively. Which one is right depends on whether the prior period is closed and whether the error is material, and the memo is the only place that judgment gets recorded.
scr_ap_reversing_an_a_p_invoice.ifSkipped: Erroneous payables inflate the aging and the expense line, and staff resort to deleting posted records, which destroys the audit trail entirely.
gaap: ASC 250 — error correction and the period of adjustment
COSO 2013 — audit trail over reversals
redFlags: Reversal dated into a period already reported to the owner
Blank or meaningless memos on reversals
Reversals of invoices that are in fact valid, used to manage a month's expense line
scr_ap_reversing_an_a_p_invoice.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > Reverse (choose reversal date and period), which posts DR 2010 A/P / CR the original expense.

scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice.purpose: Pays one invoice directly from the A/P invoices list via the Pay link — available only at Posted or Partially Paid status — selecting the bank and confirming the amount before clicking Pay now.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice.outcome: A single approved invoice is settled from the chosen bank account and closes on the vendor ledger.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice.rootCause: The bank selection on this page is the decision that matters. Every property entity has its own operating account, and choosing the wrong bank pays one owner's vendor with another owner's cash, creating an unintended intercompany advance that has to be caught, documented as a Due From and reimbursed — or it sits undetected and an owner's cash is quietly funding a property they do not own.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice.ifSkipped: Urgent single invoices wait for the next scheduled run, vendors suspend service, and late fees hit the property's expenses.
gaap: ASC 850 — related-party advances created by cross-entity payment
COSO 2013 — authorization of individual disbursements
NACHA Operating Rules — origination from the correct account
redFlags: Payment drawn on a bank belonging to a different entity than the invoice's property
Single payments used routinely to bypass the batch approval
Pay link used on invoices whose approval history is incomplete
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable > select and run Check Processing for the single payable, choosing the property's bank account.

scr_ap_printing_an_a_p_invoice_2.purpose: Prints the A/P invoice record itself as a PDF from the list, and separately opens the attached scanned vendor document through the Attachment link on the invoice information page.
scr_ap_printing_an_a_p_invoice_2.outcome: Both the system's version of the invoice and the vendor's original are printable, side by side.
scr_ap_printing_an_a_p_invoice_2.rootCause: These are two different documents and confusing them causes real errors. The printed record shows what was keyed and coded; the attachment shows what the vendor actually sent. Comparing them is the routine that catches a transposed amount, a wrong invoice number that will let a duplicate through, or a service period that puts the expense in the wrong month.
scr_ap_printing_an_a_p_invoice_2.ifSkipped: Keying errors between the vendor document and the system record go unnoticed until the vendor's statement disagrees with the aging.
gaap: COSO 2013 — accuracy and validity of recorded transactions
IRC §6001 — retention of records supporting deductions
redFlags: Keyed amount differing from the attachment
Invoices with no attachment behind them
Service period on the attachment falling outside the posted period
scr_ap_printing_an_a_p_invoice_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: print the payable from Payables > Payable and open the PAYscan invoice image from Document Management.

scr_ap_importing_an_a_p_invoice.purpose: Loads invoices from a CSV with a chosen date format and encoding, and — critically — a choice between posting to the general ledger or importing as Historical, which does not post, with an offline processing option for large files.
scr_ap_importing_an_a_p_invoice.outcome: A batch of invoices enters the system either as live payables or as non-posting history, with results emailed to the importer.
scr_ap_importing_an_a_p_invoice.rootCause: The Historical flag is the decision that goes wrong most often. On a property takeover, prior-owner invoices must load as history because the opening balance sheet already carries the payable; import them in posting mode and the acquiring entity's 2010 Accounts Payable is doubled, its expenses are overstated by a full period, and the error is not obvious because the aging looks plausible.
scr_ap_importing_an_a_p_invoice.ifSkipped: Conversion and recurring invoice volumes are keyed by hand, with the transposition rate and delay that implies at exactly the time a new property most needs accurate numbers.
gaap: COSO 2013 — completeness and accuracy of data loaded into the ledger
ASC 805 — assumed liabilities at acquisition
ASC 250 — correction of import errors
redFlags: Historical invoices imported in posting mode, doubling the opening payable
Date format mismatch shifting invoices into the wrong period
Import re-run in full after a partial failure, duplicating the successful rows
Results emailed to an address nobody monitors
scr_ap_importing_an_a_p_invoice.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Import (ETL payable import template) with a posting or non-posting load and an import error log.

scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice_2.purpose: Deletes an A/P invoice from the A/P invoices list for users holding Delete permission — an action the system withdraws entirely, including for drafts, when the application is configured to allow reversal of unpaid invoices instead.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice_2.outcome: Either the invoice is removed, or the configuration has already forced the organization onto reversals, which is the auditable path.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice_2.rootCause: Whether Delete even appears is a configuration decision made once for the whole company, and it is a control decision disguised as a preference. Turning on reversal of unpaid invoices removes deletion as an option and guarantees every payable that ever existed leaves a trace — which is what an owner's auditor expects and what a company relying on Delete cannot provide.
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice_2.ifSkipped: Erroneous and duplicate invoices remain in the aging, overstating the liability and the amount the owner believes is committed.
gaap: COSO 2013 — configuration of application controls over record removal
SOC 1 — permission assignment for destructive actions
redFlags: Delete permission held broadly across the A/P team
Deletion used rather than reversal where both are technically possible
No log reviewed for deletions in the period
scr_ap_deleting_an_a_p_invoice_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: unposted payables can be deleted; posted ones require Reverse, and the delete right is controlled through Administration > Security.

scr_ap_importing_vendors.purpose: Bulk loads vendor master records from the downloaded vendor template — including preferred payment method and, for multi-entity companies, vendor visibility and restriction data — ignoring any row beginning with a # symbol.
scr_ap_importing_vendors.outcome: A populated vendor master with the right visibility per entity, ready for invoice entry without weeks of manual setup.
scr_ap_importing_vendors.rootCause: Vendor visibility is the part that gets skipped. In a multi-entity portfolio, importing every vendor as visible to every entity means a site accountant can code an invoice to a vendor that belongs to a different owner's property, and a vendor imported without its 1099 flag or W-9 becomes a January discovery when the year's payments are already made and backup withholding was never applied.
scr_ap_importing_vendors.ifSkipped: Vendors are keyed one at a time during a takeover, go-live slips, and the first month's invoices are entered against hastily created duplicate vendor records.
gaap: IRC §6041 — vendor tax identity captured before payments begin
IRC §3406 — backup withholding where the TIN is missing
COSO 2013 — master data completeness and accuracy at conversion
redFlags: All vendors imported visible to all entities
Imported vendors with blank TIN or 1099 flag
Duplicate vendor records created because the source system's IDs were not mapped
The # comment convention used for live data rows, which silently drops them
scr_ap_importing_vendors.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Import vendor ETL template, with property-list visibility controlled through vendor setup.

scr_ap_configuring_vendor_records_for_jo.purpose: Sets both payees' names in the Print as field on the vendor record and on the Pay to contact so a single check is issued payable to two parties who must both endorse it.
scr_ap_configuring_vendor_records_for_jo.outcome: Checks that physically cannot be negotiated by one party alone, because both signatures are required.
scr_ap_configuring_vendor_records_for_jo.rootCause: Joint checks exist to defeat a specific property risk: a general contractor takes the owner's money and does not pay its subcontractor, and the subcontractor then liens the property even though the owner paid in full. Naming both the GC and the sub on the instrument means the sub is paid at the moment the GC is, which is the practical defence against a mechanic's lien on an asset the owner already paid for.
scr_ap_configuring_vendor_records_for_jo.ifSkipped: The property pays the contractor, the subcontractor goes unpaid and files a lien, and the owner pays for the same work twice to clear title.
gaap: State mechanic's lien statutes — joint check rule and lien waiver exchange
UCC Article 3 — instruments payable to two parties
COSO 2013 — payee controls over disbursements
redFlags: Joint check configured on the vendor without the subcontractor's conditional lien waiver on file
Print as name changed back to a single payee after one joint check
Joint check arrangements used without written agreement among all three parties
scr_ap_configuring_vendor_records_for_jo.yardi: Yardi Voyager: joint payee handled through the payable's pay-to / remit-to name and check print name, with lien waivers tracked in Job Cost.

scr_ap_setting_up_payment_information_fo.purpose: Configures the vendor's Payment Information tab — automatic payment notification plus the electronic payment format and SEC code, choosing Personal (PPD) for an individual contractor's personal account or Business (CTX or CCD) as the bank directs, for US vendors payable in USD.
scr_ap_setting_up_payment_information_fo.outcome: The vendor is set to receive funds electronically under the correct NACHA entry class and to be notified automatically when payment is confirmed.
scr_ap_setting_up_payment_information_fo.rootCause: The PPD versus CCD/CTX choice is not cosmetic. NACHA treats a debit or credit to a consumer account differently from one to a corporate account, including the return window, so a handyman's personal account coded as CCD can be returned by the receiving bank and the payment quietly fails — leaving the invoice marked paid, the vendor unpaid and the cash still in the property's account at reconciliation time.
scr_ap_setting_up_payment_information_fo.ifSkipped: Electronic payments are returned or rejected, vendors chase payments the system shows as settled, and A/P spends the month reconciling failures.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — SEC codes PPD, CCD and CTX and return timeframes
COSO 2013 — validation of vendor payment instructions
IRC §6041 — vendor identity consistency with 1099 reporting
redFlags: Individual contractors coded as CCD business entries
Bank details entered from an emailed request with no call-back verification
Notification enabled with no email address on the Pay to contact
Foreign vendors set up under a US ACH format
scr_ap_setting_up_payment_information_fo.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor > EFT tab (routing, account, SEC class) with ACH origination configured on Setup > Bank.

scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_ledger_for_one_ve.purpose: Opens the A/P ledger report filtered to a single vendor from the Vendors list; in multi-currency companies it requires a location or location group to be chosen through Customize before it will render.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_ledger_for_one_ve.outcome: Every invoice, credit, payment and adjustment for one vendor in one chronological view.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_ledger_for_one_ve.rootCause: Vendor statement reconciliation is done here, and it is the control that catches what the aging cannot: a duplicate invoice keyed under a slightly different number, a credit memo the vendor issued that was never entered, or payments applied to the wrong invoices so both sides show the right total but disagree line by line. The location requirement in multi-currency setups also means a portfolio-wide vendor must be reviewed per location group or the picture is partial.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_ledger_for_one_ve.ifSkipped: Vendor disputes escalate without a shared record, duplicate invoices stay in the aging, and outstanding credits are never claimed.
gaap: COSO 2013 — subledger reconciliation to third-party records
ASC 405 — measurement of outstanding obligations
redFlags: Debit balances on a vendor, meaning the property has overpaid
Multi-currency ledger reviewed for one location while activity exists in others
Invoice numbers differing only by punctuation, which is the duplicate-payment signature
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_ledger_for_one_ve.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor > Ledger / vendor payable history, or Analytics > Payable Analytics filtered to the vendor.

scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_for.purpose: Enables EFT (Standard 005) or BACS on a vendor's Payment Information tab with branch ID and account number, available only where the multi-currency feature is switched on, for vendors paid outside the US ACH network.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_for.outcome: Cross-border vendors are payable electronically in the correct national format instead of by international wire.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_for.rootCause: Foreign payment formats carry different identifiers and different failure modes than ACH — a BACS sort code or a Canadian branch ID has no US routing-number equivalent, and a wrong digit produces a rejected or misdirected payment that takes weeks and correspondent-bank fees to recover. Paying a foreign vendor also raises whether withholding and Form 1042-S reporting apply rather than the 1099 the US template assumes.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_for.ifSkipped: Cross-border vendors are paid by wire at high per-transaction cost, or by a misformatted file that the receiving bank rejects.
gaap: IRC §1441 / Form 1042-S — withholding and reporting on payments to foreign persons
OFAC sanctions screening on cross-border payments
ASC 830 — foreign currency transaction measurement
redFlags: Foreign vendors set up without W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E on file
Branch ID or sort code entered without bank confirmation
Cross-border payments made without OFAC screening
Multi-currency vendors flagged for 1099 rather than 1042-S
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_for.yardi: Yardi Voyager (international): Payables > Vendor EFT/BACS bank details with multi-currency enabled and payment files generated per country format.

scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_account_numbe.purpose: Generates a supplier account number per property against a vendor's Storefront supplier code so site teams can order from catalogs, requiring both an entity address and a shipping address on the property and returning Declined where the supplier has marked the account Do Not Service.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_account_numbe.outcome: Each property has its own account with the supplier, so catalog orders and the resulting invoices carry the right property from the outset.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_account_numbe.rootCause: One shared supplier account across a portfolio is how catalog spend becomes unallocable — the supplier invoices a single account, the invoice arrives without a property, and someone splits it by guesswork at month end. A per-property account number means the supplier's own billing already carries the entity, so the invoice codes itself and the owner's expense is right without an allocation.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_account_numbe.ifSkipped: Catalog purchases arrive on one consolidated invoice with no property identification and are allocated by estimate, distorting every property's supply expense.
gaap: COSO 2013 — accuracy of cost attribution by entity
ASC 850 — avoiding unsupported cost sharing between affiliated entities
redFlags: Account requests Declined and left unresolved, pushing orders back to a shared account
Properties missing a shipping address so the request cannot be generated
Shared supplier accounts still in use after per-property numbers were issued
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_account_numbe.yardi: Yardi Marketplace: per-property supplier accounts and punchout catalogs feeding Procure to Pay purchase orders.

scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_rem.purpose: Turns on the Use Remittance email address option in the vendor's Primary contact section, accepting multiple semicolon-separated addresses and a chosen attachment format of PDF or Excel for the remittance detail.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_rem.outcome: Vendors receive machine-readable remittance detail at their AR mailbox when payment is made.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_rem.rootCause: Remittance detail is what lets a vendor apply the payment to the right invoices on their side. A lump ACH with no remittance gets posted on account, the vendor's statement still shows the invoices open, and the property receives a dunning notice for invoices it has already paid — which then consumes A/P time reconciling a dispute that the remittance email would have prevented entirely.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_rem.ifSkipped: Vendors misapply payments, statements disagree with the property's aging, and paid invoices are chased as delinquent.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — remittance information accompanying ACH credits
COSO 2013 — external confirmation of settled obligations
redFlags: Remittance sent to a sales contact rather than the vendor's AR mailbox
Semicolon list containing a departed employee's address
Remittance enabled on vendors whose payments are still made by check with the stub already attached
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_to_receive_rem.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor remittance email address with emailed remittance advice on EFT/check runs, or VendorCafe self-service remittance.

scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_join_the_netw.purpose: Sends an invitation from the vendor record inviting the vendor to join the RealPage vendor community; on acceptance the system assigns the vendor a Storefront Supplier Code, which is the prerequisite for catalog use.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_join_the_netw.outcome: The vendor becomes transactable through the network, with its own maintained profile and catalog access.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_join_the_netw.rootCause: Network onboarding shifts who maintains the vendor's remit-to and bank details from the A/P clerk to the vendor itself, behind the vendor's own authentication. That is the single most effective control against business email compromise, where a spoofed email asks A/P to change a vendor's bank account and the money goes to the fraudster on the next run.
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_join_the_netw.ifSkipped: Vendor detail changes keep arriving by email and are keyed on trust, leaving the portfolio exposed to payment-redirection fraud.
gaap: COSO 2013 — fraud risk over vendor master changes
SOC 1 — third-party onboarding within the control environment
IRC §6041 — W-9 collection during onboarding
redFlags: Invitations sent to an email address supplied in the same message that requested a bank change
Vendors transacting at volume with no network enrollment and no verified profile
Supplier codes assigned without W-9 and insurance on file
scr_ap_requesting_a_vendor_join_the_netw.yardi: Yardi VendorCafe: vendor self-service onboarding, compliance document upload and maintained payment profiles feeding Voyager Payables.

scr_ap_setting_up_a_vendor_for_one_time_.purpose: Flags a vendor as One-time on the Vendor tab so it is hidden from the standard vendor list unless specifically filtered for, with the flag removable later if the relationship turns out to be ongoing.
scr_ap_setting_up_a_vendor_for_one_time_.outcome: A clean working vendor list for routine coding, with the rarely used records still present and findable.
scr_ap_setting_up_a_vendor_for_one_time_.rootCause: The flag keeps a resident refund payee or a single emergency plumber out of the lookup that A/P uses fifty times a day, which reduces miscoding. But hidden is not exempt: a one-time vendor paid over the IRC §6041 threshold still requires a 1099, and because it never appears in routine vendor reviews it is the record most likely to reach year-end with no W-9 and no TIN.
scr_ap_setting_up_a_vendor_for_one_time_.ifSkipped: The vendor list fills with single-use payees, the correct vendor becomes hard to find, and mis-selection on invoice coding rises.
gaap: IRC §6041 — reporting applies regardless of how the vendor is flagged
IRC §3406 — backup withholding where no TIN was collected
COSO 2013 — completeness of vendor master review
redFlags: One-time vendors with cumulative payments over the 1099 threshold
The flag used to keep a recurring vendor out of periodic master reviews
One-time vendors with bank details on file
scr_ap_setting_up_a_vendor_for_one_time_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor with a one-time/temporary vendor type excluded from the default lookup but included in 1099 processing.

scr_ap_making_a_vendor_a_child_of_anothe.purpose: Selects a parent on the Additional Information tab so vendors sit in a hierarchy — regional branches under a national supplier, operating subsidiaries under a holding company.
scr_ap_making_a_vendor_a_child_of_anothe.outcome: Related vendor records roll up to one parent for spend visibility and reporting, while each branch keeps its own remit-to.
scr_ap_making_a_vendor_a_child_of_anothe.rootCause: Spend concentration is invisible without the hierarchy. Fifteen branch records of one national supplier each look like a modest vendor, but rolled up they may be the portfolio's largest payee — which is the number that matters for negotiating a national pricing agreement, for assessing concentration risk if that supplier fails mid-renovation, and for 1099 reporting where the parent's TIN, not the branch's, is the reportable identity.
scr_ap_making_a_vendor_a_child_of_anothe.ifSkipped: Portfolio spend with a single corporate group is fragmented across records, national pricing leverage is lost, and concentration risk goes unmeasured.
gaap: IRC §6041 — reporting under the payee's correct legal TIN
COSO 2013 — vendor master organization supporting spend analysis
ASC 450 — concentration and supplier dependency considerations
redFlags: Child vendors carrying different TINs from the parent where the parent is the legal payee
Hierarchies built on trade names rather than legal entities
Parent assigned without confirming the corporate relationship still exists after an acquisition
scr_ap_making_a_vendor_a_child_of_anothe.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor parent/child association on the vendor record, used for consolidated vendor spend reporting.

scr_ap_1099_vendor_information.purpose: The vendor-level 1099 configuration area where a vendor is tagged reportable, a form type and default box are set, historical year-to-date amounts can be seeded for a mid-year setup, and each subsequent transaction line inherits the form and box.
scr_ap_1099_vendor_information.outcome: Reportable payments accumulate automatically against the right form and box from the moment the vendor is tagged.
scr_ap_1099_vendor_information.rootCause: The historical YTD field exists because vendors are routinely set up mid-year or a property is taken over mid-year, and the payments made before the changeover are still the owner's reportable payments for the calendar year. Without seeding them, the January 1099 reports only the stub period, the vendor's own records disagree, and the IRS receives an understated information return.
scr_ap_1099_vendor_information.ifSkipped: 1099 totals capture only payments made after the vendor was tagged, producing understated returns and penalty exposure under IRC §6721.
gaap: IRC §6041 — information returns for payments in the course of a trade or business
IRC §6721/§6722 — penalties for incorrect or incomplete returns
IRC §3406 — backup withholding
redFlags: Mid-year vendor setups with no historical YTD seeded
Prior-manager payments omitted from the takeover year's totals
Line-level form and box overrides used inconsistently across a vendor's invoices
scr_ap_1099_vendor_information.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor 1099 settings with 1099 adjustments entered for prior-period amounts before 1099 Processing.

scr_ap_editing_1099_information_for_an_e.purpose: Changes an existing vendor's 1099 name and form selection — MISC, INT, DIV, R, S, PATR or G — where the 1099 name prints above the Print as name whenever the two differ.
scr_ap_editing_1099_information_for_an_e.outcome: The vendor's reportable identity and form type reflect the legal payee rather than the trade name used operationally.
scr_ap_editing_1099_information_for_an_e.rootCause: The split between the 1099 name and the Print as name is the mechanism that makes TIN matching work. A property pays 'Sunrise Landscaping' but the TIN belongs to 'J. Alvarez Enterprises LLC'; report the trade name against that TIN and the IRS TIN match fails, a CP2100 notice follows, and the payer must begin backup withholding at 24% on a vendor that was never actually non-compliant.
scr_ap_editing_1099_information_for_an_e.ifSkipped: Name and TIN combinations mismatch at filing, B notices arrive, and the property becomes liable for backup withholding it never deducted.
gaap: IRS TIN matching program — name/TIN combination validation
IRC §3406 — backup withholding following a B notice
IRC §6722 — payee statement penalties
redFlags: 1099 name left as the DBA when the W-9 names an LLC or individual
Form type changed late in the year without reviewing the transactions already coded
Vendor edits made without the current W-9 in hand
scr_ap_editing_1099_information_for_an_e.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor > 1099 name and form type, validated against the W-9 before 1099 Processing runs.

scr_ap_form_1099_information_with_defaul.purpose: The page where the default 1099 form and box are chosen for a vendor, reached from the Additional Information tab, exposing extra fields beneath the selection and — for multi-entity companies — an Entity field that scopes the setting.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_with_defaul.outcome: Every transaction against the vendor defaults to the right box, per entity where the company is multi-entity.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_with_defaul.rootCause: The Entity field is what separates this from a simple default. Each property-owning LP or LLC files its own 1099s under its own EIN, so the same landscaper paid by four entities generates four returns. Setting the form and box without scoping the entity means the amounts either merge under one filer or split unpredictably, and the vendor receives statements that do not match any single payer's records.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_with_defaul.ifSkipped: Box assignments are made by hand on each invoice line, coding drifts across the year, and the 1099 file has to be rebuilt from the payment register in January.
gaap: IRC §6041 — payer-level reporting by filing entity
ASC 810 — separate reporting obligations of each legal entity
IRC §6721 — accuracy penalties
redFlags: Entity field left blank in a multi-entity company
Attorney payments defaulted to a non-legal box
Default box chosen once and never revisited when the vendor's services changed
scr_ap_form_1099_information_with_defaul.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor 1099 form/box default with 1099 processing run per filing entity and EIN.

scr_ap_adding_the_1099_status_to_a_vendo.purpose: Adds 1099 status to a vendor that was set up without it, selecting form, default box and paying entity, then offering to update the line items on that vendor's existing transactions — with the bulk alternative of exporting via the 1099 report and re-importing through the vendor 1099 transaction update template.
scr_ap_adding_the_1099_status_to_a_vendo.outcome: A vendor that should have been reportable all along has both its master record and its already-posted transaction lines corrected.
scr_ap_adding_the_1099_status_to_a_vendo.rootCause: Flagging the vendor prospectively does nothing for the payments already made, and those are usually most of the year. The retroactive line-item update is the whole point of the screen — without it, a contractor who was set up as non-reportable in February and corrected in November is reported on two months of payments, while the IRS receives nothing for the other nine.
scr_ap_adding_the_1099_status_to_a_vendo.ifSkipped: The vendor's prior payments stay unflagged, the 1099 understates by the bulk of the year, and the correction becomes an amended return.
gaap: IRC §6041 — full-year reportable payments
IRC §6721 — penalties for understated information returns
COSO 2013 — completeness of retroactive data corrections
redFlags: Status added without running the before-and-after 1099 report to confirm the transaction count changed
Bulk template re-import applied to the wrong tax year
Retroactive update declined at the prompt and then forgotten
scr_ap_adding_the_1099_status_to_a_vendo.yardi: Yardi Voyager: set the vendor 1099 flag and post 1099 adjustments for prior payments, verified through the 1099 Report before filing.

scr_ap_removing_a_vendors_1099_status.purpose: Clears a vendor's 1099 status by setting Form Name to None — which must actually be cleared and saved or it reappears — and then optionally strips the 1099 status from line items on that vendor's existing A/P invoices, with the 1099 detail report run before and after to size the change.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendors_1099_status.outcome: A vendor correctly identified as non-reportable stops accumulating 1099 amounts, and its historical lines are cleaned if that is intended.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendors_1099_status.rootCause: Removing status is far riskier than adding it, because the failure is silent: the vendor simply never appears on the 1099 run and nobody notices an absence. Corporations are generally exempt, but attorneys are reportable even when incorporated and medical payments have their own rule, so a well-meaning cleanup that de-flags the eviction law firm produces a missing return the IRS will notice and the property will not.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendors_1099_status.ifSkipped: Exempt corporate vendors keep accumulating 1099 amounts and receive returns they should not, generating vendor disputes and pointless corrections.
gaap: IRC §6041A — attorney payments reportable regardless of incorporation
IRC §6721 — penalties for failure to file required returns
COSO 2013 — review before destructive master-data change
redFlags: Attorney or law firm vendors de-flagged as incorporated
Form Name not actually cleared, so the setting silently returns
Historical line items stripped for a year already filed
Removal performed without the before-and-after report comparison
scr_ap_removing_a_vendors_1099_status.yardi: Yardi Voyager: clear the vendor's 1099 type and reverse prior 1099 adjustments, re-running the 1099 Report to confirm the effect.

scr_ap_setting_up_the_vendor_to_use_the_.purpose: Marks a vendor as CA DE 542 required on the Additional Information tab and records the Date sent, with the system validating that the country is US before the form will print.
scr_ap_setting_up_the_vendor_to_use_the_.outcome: California independent contractor reporting is triggered for the vendors it applies to, with the submission date on record.
scr_ap_setting_up_the_vendor_to_use_the_.rootCause: California requires a service-recipient to report an independent contractor to the EDD within twenty days of paying or contracting for $600 or more — a deadline measured from the engagement, not from year end, and enforced separately from federal 1099 reporting. An owner with California assets who tracks only 1099s has already missed it by the time January arrives, and the per-failure penalties accrue by contractor.
scr_ap_setting_up_the_vendor_to_use_the_.ifSkipped: California EDD contractor reports are filed late or not at all, exposing the owner to per-contractor penalties independent of any 1099 compliance.
gaap: California Unemployment Insurance Code §1088.8 — DE 542 independent contractor reporting
IRC §6041 — parallel federal information reporting
COSO 2013 — compliance monitoring by jurisdiction
redFlags: California contractors paid over $600 with the DE 542 flag never set
Date sent left blank after the form was filed
Vendor country entered in a format the validation rejects, silently suppressing the form
Reliance on the 1099 population, which misses contractors engaged but not yet paid
scr_ap_setting_up_the_vendor_to_use_the_.yardi: No dedicated DE 542 function in Yardi Voyager; California contractor reporting is produced from vendor and payment data outside the 1099 process.

scr_ap_listing_vendors_that_lack_w9_atta.purpose: Builds a custom Vendors view that includes the Attachments column and sorts on it, so vendors with no attached W-9 group together and can be worked as a list.
scr_ap_listing_vendors_that_lack_w9_atta.outcome: A worklist of vendors whose tax documentation is missing, produced without any special report.
scr_ap_listing_vendors_that_lack_w9_atta.rootCause: Backup withholding obligation attaches at the moment of payment, not at year end. Every vendor on this list that is being paid represents a payment the property should arguably have withheld 24% from under IRC §3406, and the exposure is the payer's, not the vendor's — so the list is best run before a check run rather than in December when a year of unwithheld payments is already out the door.
scr_ap_listing_vendors_that_lack_w9_atta.ifSkipped: Vendors are paid without a W-9 on file, the payer carries the unremitted backup withholding liability, and January 1099s are filed with missing or invented TINs.
gaap: IRC §3406 — backup withholding where the payee's TIN is not on file
IRS Form W-9 — solicitation and retention requirements
IRC §6721/§6722 — return and payee statement penalties
redFlags: Active vendors with payment volume and no W-9 attachment
Attachments present but named so poorly that the W-9 cannot be identified
The list run only at year end rather than before payment runs
Single scan upload leaving files under system-generated names
scr_ap_listing_vendors_that_lack_w9_atta.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor list filtered on missing Document Management attachments, or VendorCafe compliance tracking of W-9 status.

scr_ap_setting_a_vendors_preferred_payme.purpose: Sets the default payment method on a vendor's Payment Information tab, which then pre-populates the method on both the Pay A/P Invoices page and the Group by entity page.
scr_ap_setting_a_vendors_preferred_payme.outcome: Payment runs default each vendor to the method that vendor actually accepts, with the default still overridable on the run.
scr_ap_setting_a_vendors_preferred_payme.rootCause: The default is where check-versus-ACH economics get decided for the portfolio. A check costs several dollars in stock, postage and handling and takes days to clear; an ACH costs cents and settles predictably, which materially improves the accuracy of the property's cash forecast. The same default is also a fraud surface — a vendor silently switched from check to ACH just before a run sends funds to whichever account is on file.
scr_ap_setting_a_vendors_preferred_payme.ifSkipped: Every payment run requires manual method selection per vendor, defaults drift, and vendors set up for ACH still receive checks.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — authorization for electronic credits to the vendor
COSO 2013 — change control over payment instructions
redFlags: Payment method changed within days of a check run
Vendors defaulted to ACH with no bank details on file, so payments fall out of the run
Method changes made by the same user who releases payments
scr_ap_setting_a_vendors_preferred_payme.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor payment method default (check/EFT) driving selection in Check Processing and EFT runs.

scr_ap_creating_a_vendor_record_for_an_e.purpose: Creates a vendor record typed as Employee — ID, name, primary contact and payment method — because an employee cannot be reimbursed until such a record exists, and it is the prerequisite for the expense report approval configuration that follows.
scr_ap_creating_a_vendor_record_for_an_e.outcome: An employee payee exists that expense reports can be paid against, separate from payroll.
scr_ap_creating_a_vendor_record_for_an_e.rootCause: Employee reimbursements move through A/P but are not vendor spend, and the distinction is what keeps two things straight: the liability belongs in 2150 Employee Reimbursements Payable rather than trade payables, and reimbursements of substantiated business expenses under an accountable plan are not 1099 or W-2 reportable — so typing the record as Employee is what stops a maintenance tech's mileage reimbursement appearing on a 1099-NEC.
scr_ap_creating_a_vendor_record_for_an_e.ifSkipped: Employees are set up as ordinary vendors, reimbursements land in trade payables and may be reported as contractor income on a 1099.
gaap: IRC §62(c) / Treas. Reg. §1.62-2 — accountable plan reimbursements excluded from reportable income
IRC §6041 — employees are not 1099 payees
COSO 2013 — segregation of employee payees from trade vendors
redFlags: Employee vendors not typed as Employee, so they enter the 1099 population
Employee vendor records left active after termination
Reimbursements paid without receipts, which breaks accountable plan treatment
Bank details for an employee vendor matching a vendor already on file
scr_ap_creating_a_vendor_record_for_an_e.yardi: Yardi Voyager: employee set up as a Payables vendor for reimbursements (no native expense module), paid through Payable Entry or PAYscan.

scr_ap_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.purpose: Selects an override G/L account under Billing details on the vendor's Additional Information tab, after which every transaction created for that vendor defaults its coding to that account.
scr_ap_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.outcome: Single-purpose vendors code themselves correctly with no reliance on the person keying the invoice.
scr_ap_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.rootCause: A default is only as good as its fit. It genuinely helps where a vendor does exactly one thing — the water utility to 6210, the insurance broker to 6610 — but a vendor who does both routine repairs and a full unit renovation will default the renovation to 6110 Repairs & Maintenance, and a capital project quietly expensed that way understates the asset basis, overstates operating expense and distorts NOI in the year the owner is least willing to see it.
scr_ap_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.ifSkipped: Every invoice for a single-purpose vendor is coded by hand and the account drifts, producing variance noise the property manager has to explain each month.
gaap: ASC 360 — capitalization of improvements versus expensing of repairs
COSO 2013 — application controls over default coding
redFlags: Override set on contractors who perform both capital and expense work
Overrides pointing at a balance sheet account nobody reconciles
Defaults accepted on renovation invoices without a capitalization review
scr_ap_setting_up_an_alternative_g_l_acc.yardi: Yardi Voyager: default expense account on the vendor record, overridden per payable detail line where the work is capital.

scr_ap_enabling_vendors_to_receive_ach_o.purpose: Enables electronic payment on a vendor by selecting ACH, EFT or BACS as the bank format and entering the routing number, account number, account type and account classification of personal or business — with bulk loading available through the vendor electronic payment import.
scr_ap_enabling_vendors_to_receive_ach_o.outcome: The vendor is payable electronically with complete, correctly classified banking instructions.
scr_ap_enabling_vendors_to_receive_ach_o.rootCause: This screen is the highest-value target in the entire A/P module for business email compromise. A fraudster needs only one convincing email to get a routing and account number changed here, and the next payment run sends the property's cash to them irreversibly — ACH credits are not recallable once settled. The call-back verification to a number from the vendor master, never from the request, is the only control that reliably stops it.
scr_ap_enabling_vendors_to_receive_ach_o.ifSkipped: Vendors are paid by check at higher cost and slower settlement, and bank detail changes continue to be accepted on email trust.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — account validation and origination requirements
COSO 2013 — fraud risk over changes to payment instructions
SOC 1 — logging and review of vendor bank detail changes
redFlags: Bank details changed on the basis of an emailed request alone
Personal accounts classified as business, which changes the return window
The Bank Details permission granted to the same users who release payment runs
Bulk electronic payment imports applied without a change review
scr_ap_enabling_vendors_to_receive_ach_o.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor > EFT tab bank details, permission-controlled, with ACH origination configured on Setup > Bank.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_payment_informa.purpose: The Payment Information tab itself, holding three sections — Payment details including preferred method and the Merge payment requests option, Payment services for electronic payment and notification, and Vendor account number — and hidden entirely from users without the Bank details permission.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_payment_informa.outcome: One tab governing how a vendor gets paid, visible only to staff cleared to see and change banking instructions.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_payment_informa.rootCause: The Merge payment requests setting on this tab quietly decides the shape of the disbursement. Merged, a vendor with twelve invoices across eight properties receives one payment and one remittance; unmerged, it receives twelve. Merged payments are cheaper and cleaner but obscure the per-property detail unless the remittance carries it, and if the merge crosses entities the single payment draws one property's cash to settle another's invoices.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_payment_informa.ifSkipped: Payment behaviour is set ad hoc at each run, remittance detail is inconsistent, and banking fields end up visible to staff who should not see them.
gaap: SOC 1 — restricted access to vendor bank details
NACHA Operating Rules — remittance accompanying merged credits
