ASC 850 — intercompany effect of cross-entity merged payments
redFlags: Merged payment requests spanning entities without intercompany entries
Bank details permission granted broadly rather than to a named few
Preferred method and electronic setup disagreeing, so payments fall out of the run
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_payment_informa.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor payment/EFT tabs with the corresponding bank-detail security rights in Administration > Security.

scr_ap_payment_requests_and_posted_payme.purpose: Explains the distinction between a payment request, which has been created but has not posted and may still be sitting in the approval queue, and a posted payment, which has hit the ledger.
scr_ap_payment_requests_and_posted_payme.outcome: Clarity on which disbursements have actually affected cash and which are still proposals.
scr_ap_payment_requests_and_posted_payme.rootCause: Treating a request as a payment is how cash forecasts go wrong. The request commits nothing — it can be cancelled, edited or stall indefinitely behind an approver on leave — yet it looks like a payment on screen. At period end the population that matters is the requests still unapproved: the invoices behind them remain open payables and belong in 2010 Accounts Payable, not netted against cash.
scr_ap_payment_requests_and_posted_payme.ifSkipped: Unposted requests are counted as paid, the cash position is understated, the payables balance is wrong, and vendors chase invoices the team believes are settled.
gaap: ASC 405 — a liability is derecognized only when settled
COSO 2013 — cut-off between committed and completed disbursements
redFlags: Payment requests aging in the approval queue past vendor terms
Cash forecasts built on requests rather than posted payments
Requests for a period that has since closed
scr_ap_payment_requests_and_posted_payme.yardi: Yardi Voyager: unposted check batches and pending EFT runs versus posted checks in the Check Register.

scr_ap_pay_a_p_invoices_outbox.purpose: A per-user holding area for draft payment requests, letting the accountant assemble requests across different banks and currencies, see the total of everything staged, and hold them until ready to process.
scr_ap_pay_a_p_invoices_outbox.outcome: A staged set of draft payments whose total can be checked against the aging before anything is released.
scr_ap_pay_a_p_invoices_outbox.rootCause: The manual's own framing — that the outbox makes tying to an aging report straightforward — is the whole point. The staged total is the last opportunity to compare what is about to leave the bank against the open payables it is meant to settle, before the money moves. It is also a private workspace, so drafts left staged by an accountant who is on leave are invisible to everyone else, and the vendors behind them simply go unpaid.
scr_ap_pay_a_p_invoices_outbox.ifSkipped: Payment requests are released piecemeal with no aggregate check against the aging or against available cash, one bank at a time.
gaap: COSO 2013 — review of the complete disbursement proposal before release
ASC 405 — obligations remain until the payment is processed
redFlags: Drafts aging in one user's outbox with no visibility to the team
Outbox total not tied to the aging before processing
Drafts staged against banks with insufficient available cash
Mixed-currency drafts processed without confirming the rate applied
scr_ap_pay_a_p_invoices_outbox.yardi: Yardi Voyager: unposted check batches held in Check Processing until reviewed and posted, with batch totals visible before printing.

scr_ap_releasing_for_payment.purpose: Releases items for payment at either the invoice level or the individual line item level, a permission-gated feature that must be enabled before it can be used.
scr_ap_releasing_for_payment.outcome: Only the approved portion of an invoice becomes payable, while the disputed or unverified portion stays held.
scr_ap_releasing_for_payment.rootCause: Line-level release exists for the partially disputed invoice, which is routine in property operations — a contractor bills for eight unit turns and the property manager can verify six. Releasing only the verified lines pays what is owed and keeps the dispute open on the rest, instead of the two bad choices that would otherwise apply: hold the whole invoice and age the contractor out, or pay it all and try to claw back later.
scr_ap_releasing_for_payment.ifSkipped: Whole invoices are held over a disputed line, vendors stop work on partial-payment grounds, or the full amount is paid and the dispute becomes a recovery effort.
gaap: COSO 2013 — authorization at the level of the verified obligation
ASC 450 — treatment of the disputed portion as a contingency
State prompt-payment statutes on undisputed amounts
redFlags: Line-level release rights granted to users without invoice approval authority
Released lines that were never actually verified against the work order
Held lines aging indefinitely with no dispute resolution
Release used to split an invoice below an approval threshold
scr_ap_releasing_for_payment.yardi: Yardi Voyager: payable hold/release at the payable and detail-line level, driven by PAYscan workflow approval rights.

scr_ap_stopping_payments.purpose: The map of the several ways a payment can be stopped depending on how far it has travelled — removing an invoice from a draft request, removing the draft request from the outbox, cancelling a payment request, stopping an AvidXchange payment, or placing the invoice on hold.
scr_ap_stopping_payments.outcome: The accountant picks the right intervention for where the payment currently sits, instead of trying one that no longer applies.
scr_ap_stopping_payments.rootCause: Stopping a payment is a race against its own processing, and the window narrows at each stage. An invoice can be pulled from a draft in seconds; once the request is submitted only cancellation works; once it reaches the payment processor only that processor's stop applies; once the ACH has settled nothing stops it and recovery becomes a request to the receiving bank. Knowing which stage applies is the difference between a clean stop and an unrecoverable payment.
scr_ap_stopping_payments.ifSkipped: The wrong stop method is attempted, the window closes while it fails, and a payment that should have been halted settles.
gaap: UCC Article 4 — stop-payment orders on checks
NACHA Operating Rules — limited reversal window for originated entries
COSO 2013 — timely intervention on erroneous disbursements
redFlags: Stop attempted after the settlement window has closed
Stop-payment fees incurred repeatedly for the same avoidable error
Invoice placed on hold but its draft payment request left in the outbox
No record of why the payment was stopped
scr_ap_stopping_payments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: delete the unposted check batch line, void the check, or place the payable on hold; bank stop-payment handled outside Voyager.

scr_ap_payment_notifications.purpose: The vendor payment notification feature — enabling it per vendor so an email goes out whenever the system confirms a payment, maintaining the email address, determining the From contact, and notifying a vendor after the fact.
scr_ap_payment_notifications.outcome: Vendors learn of confirmed payments automatically, with the notice attributed to a real, monitored sender.
scr_ap_payment_notifications.rootCause: Notification volume is the hidden benefit: most vendor calls to A/P are 'has this been paid', and each one costs the offshore team time it does not have at close. It matters most for ACH, where nothing physical arrives and the vendor's only clue is a deposit they cannot identify. The From contact deserves thought — a notice sent from an unmonitored mailbox generates replies nobody reads, including the ones saying the payment never arrived.
scr_ap_payment_notifications.ifSkipped: The A/P inbox absorbs payment status calls all month, and ACH recipients cannot identify deposits without contacting the property.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — remittance detail with electronic credits
COSO 2013 — communication with external parties on completed transactions
redFlags: From contact set to an unmonitored mailbox
Notifications enabled on vendors with no email address captured
Notices sent for payments that subsequently failed or were voided
Vendor contact addresses never refreshed after staff turnover at the vendor
scr_ap_payment_notifications.yardi: Yardi Voyager: emailed remittance advice to the vendor's payment contact on check and EFT runs, or VendorCafe payment status self-service.

scr_ap_posted_payments.purpose: The posted payments area as a whole — viewing the list, opening a payment's details, printing a copy and exporting the list — gated by the permissions required to view posted payment records.
scr_ap_posted_payments.outcome: A defined, permission-controlled place where completed disbursements are reviewed and evidenced.
scr_ap_posted_payments.rootCause: This is the population the A/P side of the bank reconciliation is built from, so the export from here is what gets compared to the bank's cleared items. The permission gate matters as much as the data: posted payments expose payee, amount, bank and date for the whole portfolio, which is a complete map of the owner's disbursement behaviour and does not belong in front of every user with a login.
scr_ap_posted_payments.ifSkipped: There is no consolidated disbursement record to reconcile against the bank, and payment activity is reviewed one transaction at a time.
gaap: COSO 2013 — periodic independent review of disbursements
SOC 1 — access restriction over payment data
redFlags: View rights on posted payments granted portfolio-wide
Exported payment lists circulated outside the controlled environment
Posted payments with no corresponding bank activity in the following period
scr_ap_posted_payments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Register and Bank Register as the posted disbursement record, with property-list based access control.

scr_ap_proofs_of_payment.purpose: The proof-of-payment capability — searching for a specific payment or generating the RealPage Payments report — producing a document whose second page lists the invoices the payment covered.
scr_ap_proofs_of_payment.outcome: Documentary evidence that a named vendor received a specific sum against specific invoices.
scr_ap_proofs_of_payment.rootCause: The invoice list on the second page is what makes this proof rather than a receipt. A vendor claiming non-payment on invoice 4471 is not answered by showing that some money was sent; it is answered by a document naming 4471 among the invoices that payment settled. That is also the evidence an owner's counsel needs when a supplier threatens a lien on a property whose contractor was paid in full.
scr_ap_proofs_of_payment.ifSkipped: Payment disputes and lien threats are argued without documents, and the property pays a second time to make a claim go away.
gaap: State mechanic's lien statutes — evidence of payment against a claim
COSO 2013 — documentation of settled obligations
UCC Article 3 — evidence of discharge
redFlags: Proofs produced without the invoice detail page attached
Proof issued for a payment later voided or returned
Requests for proof clustering on one vendor, which usually signals a misapplication on their side
scr_ap_proofs_of_payment.yardi: Yardi Voyager: check copy plus the paid-payables detail from the Check Register as the equivalent proof-of-payment package.

scr_ap_voiding_payments.purpose: The routing guide for voiding, since where a payment is voided depends on how it was made — checks and record transfers from the Check Register, manual payments from the Manual Payments list, debit card and credit card payments from the Bank or Credit Card Register, and a paid invoice voided from the invoice itself.
scr_ap_voiding_payments.outcome: The void is performed in the register that owns the payment type, so the reversal reaches both the ledger and the bank record.
scr_ap_voiding_payments.rootCause: Voiding in the wrong place either fails or reverses only part of the transaction, leaving the invoice closed while the cash is restored, or the reverse. Payment type determines the path because each type has its own register and its own recoverability — a check can be stopped at the bank, a settled card transaction cannot — so the method dictates both where the void happens and whether a bank instruction has to accompany it.
scr_ap_voiding_payments.ifSkipped: Voids are attempted from the wrong register, reversals post partially, and cash and payables disagree until someone reconstructs the transaction by hand.
gaap: UCC Article 4 — stop-payment and void of negotiable instruments
COSO 2013 — completeness of reversal across subledger and cash
ASC 250 — period in which the correction is recorded
redFlags: Void attempted from the A/P invoice for a payment that originated in Cash Management
Void posted while the bank shows the item already cleared
Invoice status left Paid after the payment was voided
Voids dated into a closed period
scr_ap_voiding_payments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check > Void Check for checks and EFTs, with manual checks and card transactions voided from their own registers.
